thread:
sara_support: Hi team — customer Jun (acct: jun-co) reporting intermittent 500s + 15s tail latency on /v1/generate around 2026-01-12T14:03:20Z. They provided request_id: req_48f3c9e7. Can infra lookup server logs?

mike_sre: Got it. Do we have the exact timestamp from the customer? sys clocks?

sara_support: Jun said 2026-01-12 14:03:20 UTC (approx). They also sent a curl repro: 
```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"short test","request_id":"req_48f3c9e7"}'
```

jonathan_eng: Thanks. I will try a quick log search. Note retention is 30 days for hot logs; older logs may be archived.

logs-bot: FYI: logs retention policy = 30d (ELK hot), 180d (cold archive). Archived logs require ticketed retrieval.

mike_sre: Running Kibana query now. If anyone needs to run themselves: 
```
@timestamp:["2026-01-12T14:00:00" TO "2026-01-12T14:10:00"] AND json.request_id:"req_48f3c9e7"
```

jonathan_eng: If Kibana doesn't find it, try searching for trace id or client IP. Also grep raw docker logs on the node: 
```bash
sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "2026-01-12 14:00" --until "2026-01-12 14:10" | grep -i "48f3c9e7"
```

sara_support: I ran the curl repro in a sandbox and saw a 500 with body: {"error":"internal_error","request_id":"req_48f3c9e7"}. Customer willing to provide more if we need.

mike_sre: Kibana returned one match but the log event was in cold storage and truncated (no stack). Shows: 
```
2026-01-12T14:03:20.435Z INFO handler=request id=req_48f3c9e7 status=500 backend=tokenizer node=node-34 region=us-east-1
```

mike_sre: Looks like detailed payload logs were rotated off. We'll need a debug bundle from the customer for repro or request an archive pull.

jonathan_eng: Customer repro steps would help — full curl with headers, model param, content-length, and whether they used streaming. If they can capture client-side timings (tcpdump or curl -w) that'd be great.

sara_support: I'll ask Jun to run this enhanced repro that includes verbose timings and a copy of response headers: 
```bash
curl -v -w "\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: req_48f3c9e7" \
  -d '{"input":"short test","stream":false,"model":"redwood-1-small"}'
```

customer_jun: Thanks, running now. Will paste full verbose output and the response headers in a minute.

mike_sre: If Jun can't reproduce, we can file an archive retrieval. Note: archive pull ETA 24-48h and requires approval from legal for customer data. Also ping billing if they think this caused overages.

jonathan_eng: Also adding this to our internal debug checklist: check kernel OOM/kernel logs on node-34 around 14:03, check GPU memory metrics and tokenizer service restarts: 
```
kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/tokenizer --since=15m | grep "req_48f3c9e7"
```

sara_support: Jun posted verbose output: response headers include `X-Request-Id: req_48f3c9e7` and body had 500. Time_total = 15.027s. She attached a network trace (pcap) privately.

mike_sre: Good. I'll request archive retrieval with ops: ticket #OPS-4521, include request_id and pcap. Jonathan — want me to pull stacktrace once archive is back?

jonathan_eng: Yes please. If archive returns no stack, we'll ask customer for SDK version and to attempt one more run with `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` and capture stdout.

sara_support: Noted. I've told Jun expected timeline and asked for SDK + any proxy details. Will update here when they send bundle. :thumbsup:
